family.tagline: Two grandparents, one grandchild and a Companion Core in the study.
family.story: Araxi, a retired teacher, writes the parish newsletter from the study. Hagop, a retired developer, still keeps two consulting clients. Nare, eleven, studies in the small guest bedroom, and one Companion Core in the study serves the household.

members.name: Araxi
members.work: retired teacher, runs the parish newsletter

companion.name: Saffron
companion.job: Drafts the parish newsletter from the notices Araxi messages to it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Araxi reads every line and sends the newsletter herself.

companion.name: Walnut
companion.job: Drafts progress notes for Hagop’s two clients from the points he sends.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Hagop reads each note and sends it himself.

popup.title: Nare holds every door open
popup.body: Up the long brick stair, Hagop carries a parcel with a Companion Core inside. Nare runs ahead to hold each door.

popup.title: Unbox the Companion Core
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Nare lines them up while Araxi sets the Core on the desk.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Hagop plugs in the cable and steps back. Nare presses the button, and the Core wakes with a Wi-Fi network of its own.

popup.title: Join it from a phone
popup.body: In the study doorway, Hagop joins the Core’s own network from his phone, then picks the home network.

popup.title: Pick the first agent and apps
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Araxi picks Hermes and Joplin Server, and Hagop adds Forgejo. Then the two of them walk away.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Saffron says hello
popup.body: Araxi messages the agent she named after her favourite spice, and Saffron answers from the Core.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: araxi
say.text: Hello, Araxi. I am Saffron. Where shall we start?

beats.capability: take notes and keep to-dos that sync across your devices through your own server

popup.title: A choir notice joins the notebook
popup.body: A call from the choir leader moves Thursday’s practice to the afternoon. Araxi adds it to the parish notebook in Joplin Server, which syncs her devices through the Core.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Araxi reads the draft first
popup.body: On Friday morning Araxi messages Saffron the week’s notices. Saffron drafts the newsletter on the Core’s local model, and Araxi reads it and sends it herself.

say.speaker: araxi
say.text: Your five notices are in, in order. Please read them before you send the newsletter.

beats.capability: scan and file your paperwork; it reads every page, tags it and makes it searchable

popup.title: Araxi calls the renewal date down
popup.body: Hagop calls up the stairs for a client’s renewal date. Araxi types one word into Paperless-ngx, which read the scanned pages on the Core, and calls it down.

beats.capability: the LibreOffice suite (Writer, Calc and more) in your browser

popup.title: The month’s hours become an invoice
popup.body: At month’s end Araxi takes the hours from Kimai and writes the invoice in LibreOffice, in her browser. The finished invoice is saved on the Core.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals

popup.title: Dinners fit around Hagop’s calls
popup.body: At the kitchen island, Araxi plans the week’s dinners around Hagop’s client calls. Yuvomi keeps the calendar and the meal plan in one database on the Core.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals

popup.title: A pudding sends Hagop shopping
popup.body: Friday’s pudding needs apricots, so Nare adds them to the household list in Yuvomi. Hagop picks the list up on his way out to the shop.

beats.capability: host your own git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core

popup.title: The loveseat doubles as a desk
popup.body: By noon a client wants Hagop’s reporting scripts. He pushes them to Forgejo from the loveseat. The repository sits on the Core, not on a rented code host.

beats.capability: track time per project and client, with reports

popup.title: Hagop counts an hour before lunch
popup.body: When a call with his smaller client ends, Hagop adds the hour to Kimai. A hosted timer would hold his client list. Here it stays on the Core.

beats.capability: manage and read books, comics and PDFs

popup.title: Nare reads beside Hagop
popup.body: After school Nare reads her class novel in BookLore on the loveseat, while Hagop reads his own book beside her. The family’s shelf of books is served from the Core.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Walnut leaves one date for Hagop
popup.body: Hagop messages Walnut three points for a client. Walnut drafts the note on the Core’s local model and leaves one date blank. Hagop fills it in and sends it himself.

say.speaker: hagop
say.text: Three points, three paragraphs. One date is blank, so please fill it in before sending.

beats.capability: stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: Nare picks the next clip
popup.body: On Saturday morning Nare picks a clip from Hagop’s digitised holiday tapes. Jellyfin plays it from the Core to the family room TV.

beats.capability: read Wikipedia and other reference sites offline

popup.title: Nare looks up a lighthouse lens
popup.body: On her bed, Nare looks up how a lighthouse lens turns. Kiwix answers from a Wikipedia file the Core holds, so no search engine is asked.
popup.note: The Wikipedia file is downloaded once.

beats.capability: chat with models running on your own Core, from any browser

popup.title: Araxi reads the ice answer
popup.body: Nare asks Open WebUI why ice floats, and the model runs on the Core. Araxi reads the answer with her, and Nare writes it up in Obsidian.

beats.capability: translate text and documents on your own Core

popup.title: Nare writes first and checks after
popup.body: Nare writes her Spanish pen-pal letter herself, then checks a few sentences in LibreTranslate. The Core does the translating, not a translation website.

beats.capability: a local video recorder with object detection for your IP cameras

popup.title: Hagop checks whether the lorry came
popup.body: Araxi and Hagop disagree about whether the recycling lorry came on Tuesday. Hagop checks the drive camera’s clip in Frigate, which keeps it on the Core.

popup.title: Two generations, one Core
popup.body: Two grandparents, one grandchild and one Companion Core, behind the periwinkle siding.

closing.body: Your newsletter, client files, old films and homework can sit on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: The Study has no desk item in the spec; the Core stands on its own desk there. Araxi anchors on the sofa, the room and the Core, and no beat names a second desk.

The Family Room has a loveseat, a wall TV and a ladder shelf but no desk: Hagop works from the loveseat, and Nare reads there in one beat. His other anchors are the shelf and the room. The TV beat is the Family Room TV.
The Guest Bedroom has a bed and a chest of drawers only: Nare anchors on the bed and the room, and no beat names a desk or a screen there. She is never shown asleep.
Both agents are Hermes. The chat-service note rides on ftue-hello, the first Hermes beat. Companion Memory is not named anywhere.
living-tapes assumes old holiday tapes digitised to files by the family: Jellyfin plays the family’s own files only. garden-drive assumes an IP camera the family owns (not part of the Core).
BookLore fetches covers and metadata from outside (catalog caveat), so nare-reads says the books sit on the Core and claims no more.
